# Josh Lake, joshlake.ai

> Serial entrepreneur thinking about AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence. Colorado, USA.

## About Josh Lake

Josh Lake is a serial entrepreneur, technologist, and builder. He is currently focused on AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence — what becomes possible when both get cheap and abundant. He is the founder of Electrify Everything Now (free home electrification calculators). He co-founded Elephant Energy, a home electrification platform, and served as its CTO for five years. Earlier in his career, he was Head of Operations at Nuro (autonomous delivery), COO of Evercar/Vision Fleet (shared EV fleets), and Sr. Program Manager at Amonix (concentrated solar, world-record CPV modules). He holds a B.S. in Materials Science & Engineering from MIT and a Mechanical Engineering certificate from Stanford.

## Expertise

- AI and the convergence of energy and intelligence
- Speed to power: large load interconnection, queue reform, time-to-energized for data centers
- Grid capacity and risk: interconnection risk, curtailment risk, flexible load, behind-the-meter generation
- AI data center infrastructure and energy demand growth
- AI-native services businesses: delivering professional-services scope with agent-run workflows
- Agents for operations: multi-agent systems, agentic operating systems for companies
- Home electrification: heat pumps, induction stoves, EV chargers, electrical panels, smart load management
- AI implementation in small and mid-size companies
- Climate technology and clean energy
- Autonomous vehicles and electric vehicle operations
- Startup operations, scaling, and go-to-market

### Energy → Tokens → Intelligence → Invention → Abundance
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/energy-to-abundance
- Description: Eleven observations and learnings from months of hands-on building with AI agents plus podcasts, videos, and Substacks, organized around a sequence: data centers use energy and GPUs to make tokens, models use tokens to make intelligence, humans and increasingly agents use that intelligence to invent, and invention makes abundance. (1) Capacity is the product of multipliers heading toward 1,000x and then 1,000,000x useful ability to do work: model efficiency, falling token cost, parallel agents, better memory and context, better algorithms, bigger data centers, more data, and synthetic data, each worth a multiple on its own and multiplying together while price heads to zero. The math is easy, figuring out what to do with it is hard. We are at the beginning of a Cambrian explosion of ideas, products, and services. (2) Agents are the great catalyst and the modular unit of the scientific process: loops, graphs, and a goal, with Claude Code, Grok Bot, OpenClaw, and Hermes Agent; wiring agents together with LLMs, MCPs, and APIs is manufacturing engineering, less time writing code and more time designing the line. Code replicates and runs 24/7, and automation is the on-ramp to invention. (3) The impacts of invention are unfathomable and invention will be 1,000x automation: first chat, then code, now automation and agents. Automation makes existing things cheaper while invention makes things that did not exist before. Most new invention will be combinatorial across drugs, materials, recipes, movies, and products, and the wildcard is whether the invention process itself can be automated. References Mark Zuckerberg’s essay "The Future Is For Everyone." (4) The product overhang from today’s models is enormous and will be for years: hundreds of capable models across dozens of labs (Gemini, Claude, ChatGPT, Qwen, xAI, Chinese models, open and closed, tracked on Artificial Analysis), with almost nothing built on top yet. As Nat Friedman argues, chat and coding tools and agents are barely the start. If every lab stopped training tomorrow there would still be a decade of products to build. (5) We will build 1,000x more software because we can: single-user, perfectly customized, locally run, unreviewed, disposable by design, and it may not even look like software. Excel is software with a UI good enough that the coding disappeared, and everyone is already a builder. When marginal cost hits zero you build the solution and then delete it. (6) Outcomes beat output and business models explode. A useful ladder runs inputs (hours, employees, seats, tokens), outputs (reports, messages, actions, leads), outcomes (resolved problems, completed hires, saved energy, delivered capacity), and business impact (increased profit, avoided cost, better health, faster time-to-power). The farther down the ladder, the more valuable the offering and the harder measurement, attribution, and risk-sharing become. Inside companies speed to innovate beats cost savings. Do not buy software, buy results, and AI helps define success up front and verify it was delivered. (7) Vibe-living is the ultimate luxury and the natural extension of outcomes over output: the people with access to the most abundance just request things. Name a verifiable outcome and the spend, and software, robots, and capital assemble on the fly then come apart. Verification is the whole trick. Ozempic for the physical world. (8) Agent routers and model routers become a control layer because there are too many models, agents, and tools to track by hand, routing on capability, task complexity, cost, quality, reliability, data privacy, security, scalability, and repeatability. Tokens have different flavors and costs, workflows need different latencies and uptime, and training jobs are nothing like inference jobs. Tool and agent proliferation resolves into prepackaged workflows. (9) Voice input finally works: fast, accurate, and free of the old transcription bugs, whether cross-platform like Wispr Flow or built into ChatGPT or a Tesla. Most of the piece was dictated into Claude Code, removing typing as a lifelong governor on thinking. (10) There has never been a better time to start a company: one person with a stack of agents covers what used to take a whole team, the floor to start has never been lower and the ceiling on a small team never higher. Output is nearly free now, and outcomes are the only thing left worth managing. (11) Speed to power is the limiter: every link in the sequence runs on electrons, and technically the constraint is grid connection and time. Cheap electricity is the only path forward (solar and storage, nuclear, geothermal, wind, SMRs, balcony solar), the grid has more buffer than assumed, and near-term answers include solar and batteries, flexible compute, virtual power plants, demand response, behind-the-meter gas, repurposing commercial and industrial sites with existing interconnection, modular data centers, data centers overseas, and data centers in space, rather than waiting in the interconnection queue. Energized megawatts are the binding constraint on the next decade, ahead of chips, capital, and talent. Ends on the view that an abundant future does not arrive on its own, it needs to get built, and the future is for everyone.

### A Neo-Electrification Company?
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/neo-electrification-company
- Description: Essay asking what a homeowner-centric, AI-enabled, national "neo-electrification" company would look like — one that combines heat pumps, solar and storage, electrical work, financing, incentives, field execution, and a home energy operating system. Maps the players circling the opportunity (heat pump installers like Elephant Energy, Jetson, Zero Homes, QuitCarbon, Quilt, and Forge; solar and storage platforms like Sunrun and Base Power; OEMs like Mitsubishi, Daikin, LG, and Carrier; utilities and CCAs; and smart-panel companies like SPAN). Argues AI's real value is reducing soft costs across design, incentives, marketing, commissioning, service, forecasting, working capital, and margin, and looks at European models (Aira, 1KOMMA5°, Thermondo, Enpal, Octopus). Concludes the winner will be semi-vertical, AI-enabled, nationally repeatable but locally excellent, utility-aware, and obsessed with project-level economics.

### Not All Tokens Are Equal
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/not-all-tokens-are-equal
- Description: Essay arguing that AI compute is not a single market. Maps the token economy into five workloads (capability creation, commodity batch, premium interactive, agentic outcome, local/autonomous), each with different economics, latency, geography, and power profile. Argues cheap energy and cheap intelligence are now the same race, and the next infrastructure winners will integrate compute, energy, networking, orchestration, capital, and physical deployment.

### This Is How I Would Implement AI at a 40-Person Startup
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/ai-at-a-startup
- Description: Practical playbook for implementing AI at a small (~40-person) company. Covers real leadership buy-in as prerequisite; the productivity-vs-transformation choice; standardizing on one LLM and one prototyping tool; distinguishing AI-empowered, AI-first, and AI-native; pragmatic guardrails and admitting policing is hard; solving for context before capability; crawl-walk-run maturity (agents, gems, and skills come last); treating agents like employees; restructuring roles, titles, and workflows; and building a shared culture of experimentation with leading indicators (adoption, happiness, token-maxing). Based on leading the AI rollout at Elephant Energy.

### The Electrification Sequencing Problem
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/electrification-sequencing
- Description: Decision framework for homeowners deciding what to electrify first. Covers appliance replacement timing, energy math by appliance type, panel capacity, solar sizing, and navigating the rebate landscape. Based on thousands of home electrification projects.

### You Probably Don't Need a Panel Upgrade
- URL: https://joshlake.ai/writing/panel-upgrade-myth
- Description: Deep technical guide explaining why most homes do not need a $5,000-$10,000 electrical panel upgrade to electrify. Covers NEC Section 220.87 load studies, tandem breakers, load-sharing devices, dynamic load management, subpanels, and smart panels. Profiles 12 companies building panel-avoidance technology.
